newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end bourse higher after modest rally.
newsitem.headline: German shares end bourse higher after modest rally.

text.p: German shares saw a modest rally in late bourse trade on Wednesday and the DAX index of 30 blue-chip German shares ended the day 0.75 percent higher, with a good performance from individual stocks lifting the index.
The DAX was supported earlier on by upbeat February money supply growth data and results from the Ifo business confidence survey, both taken as mildly positive signs for the economy.
Crucially, neither was seen as altering the German interest rate outlook, which most economists see as stable in the near- to mid-term.
The DAX index ended up 24.74 points at 3,315.93 points having earlier fallen briefly below the psychologically important 3,300-point level.
Traders said the forthcoming expiry of options contracts on the DAX this week was also affecting cash prices.

"This is mainly a technical reaction and it's hard to identify any clear trend. The data we saw this morning were not negative, but they were not overwhelmingly positive either," said a dealer at a large Frankfurt bank.
The data showed M3 money supply growth slowing slightly to 9.1 percent from 11.7 percent in January while the Ifo west German business climate index nudged higher to 93.6 from 93.3.
Pharmaceutical group Schering got a boost after raising its sales and earnings forecasts for 1997.
Its shares pared earlier gains to end up five pfennigs at 156.25 marks, after Schering said it expected profits to rise 10 to 15 percent this year, having earlier forecast growth below ten percent.
Steelmaker Thyssen remained suspended from trade along with rival Krupp which bid on Tuesday for Thyssen's shares.

The two companies are now discussing a possible joint initiative but the situation could revert if this plan does not go ahead. Dealers said Thyssen's shares were now trading at 430 marks in unofficial dealings.
The main boost to the index came from good individual performances in the chemical, banking and utility sectors.
